summary: Executed 20 backend integration tests for VulnScan AI covering auth (register/login/me/JWT protection), scan lifecycle (upload ZIP -> queued -> scanning -> completed, ~30s), user isolation, real findings from Semgrep+Bandit+Gitleaks+IaC+SCA (verified Kubernetes privileged/docker.sock CRITICAL, pyyaml CVE, sorted-by-severity), Claude Sonnet 4.5 AI analysis endpoint, sandboxed bash terminal (ls/pwd inside workspace, blocks shutdown/mkfs), PDF+Markdown report generation, and DELETE cleanup. 20/20 tests PASSED against the public preview URL.

minor.issue: Scan job runs via asyncio.create_task inside the FastAPI event loop (blocking IO like reportlab/semgrep run in-process). Under load or worker restart mid-scan the job is silently lost with no retry / no persistent queue. Consider background worker (RQ / Celery / arq) or at least a startup recovery for 'scanning' scans.
'vulnerabilities_indexed' is a GLOBAL count across ALL users (see server.py:397 comment 'global count for demo'). Leaks tenant data volume; should be scoped to user_id.
PDF/MD generated synchronously on each request. For large scans this ties up the event loop; consider running build_pdf in a threadpool via run_in_executor.

action_items: No functional bugs found. Suite is green.

IMPORTANT for future test agents: this suite MUST run serially. pytest.ini pins '-n 2 --dist loadscope' which splits classes to different xdist workers; because TestScanLifecycle stores scan_id as a class attribute shared with TestTerminal/TestReports/TestDelete, parallel workers make later classes fail with 404. Run with 'python -m pytest backend/tests/test_vulnscan_backend.py -n 0'. Alternatively refactor tests to use a session fixture returning scan_id (recommended).
Consider scoping /api/stats vulnerabilities_indexed to the caller instead of a global count.
Consider a durable job queue for scans so an in-flight scan survives backend restarts.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: scan pipeline is entirely in the API process (asyncio.create_task) — no persistence for interrupted scans, status stays 'scanning' forever if backend restarts.
server.py:397 exposes global vulnerabilities_indexed count across tenants — potential data leak, marked 'for demo'.

scanners.py: semgrep --config auto requires network to fetch the registry; if blocked, silently returns zero semgrep findings (still logged as 'completed'). Backend should surface this in scanner_log so users know rules were unavailable.
server.py:87 _vuln_public excludes _id but list_scans / get_vulns already project it out — minor duplication.
reports.py PDF build is synchronous CPU work in the async handler; wrap with asyncio.to_thread for larger reports.

auth.py: JWT_SECRET is read at import time via os.environ['JWT_SECRET']; if missing the module fails to import (fail-fast is fine, but should be documented). No refresh-token flow — 7-day access token is long-lived.
test_credentials: demo@vulnscan.ai / Demo1234! (verified working). Extra users are generated with test_<uuid>@vulnscan.ai / Passw0rd! during the run.
seed_data_creation: Test creates a synthetic vulnerable ZIP in-memory (app.py with subprocess/hardcoded AWS keys + path traversal, requirements.txt with pyyaml==3.13/flask==2.0.0/requests==2.25.0, k8s/pod.yaml with privileged:true+docker.sock+hostPath, .env with API_KEY) and uploads it as project 'TEST_vuln_project'. Scan+workspace are deleted at the end of the run via DELETE /api/scans/{id}.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Suite lives at /app/backend/tests/test_vulnscan_backend.py. RUN COMMAND: `python -m pytest backend/tests/test_vulnscan_backend.py -n 0 -v` from /app (the -n 0 is mandatory because tests share scan_id across classes and pytest.ini forces xdist loadscope). Full run ~75s (30-40s of it is waiting for the actual scan to finish). If you add more classes that depend on scan_id, either keep -n 0 or refactor to a session-scoped fixture that creates the scan once and yields the id.
